title: Complete rational accounts with cancellation-path equivalence and irreducible endpoints
summary: RAW_UNREVIEWED, NOT SELECTED. An owned Liber abbaci pp.50–51 construction multiplies mixed quantities by two paths: full multiplication then reduction, or exact cross-cancellation then multiplication. Its following greatest-common-measure rule distinguishes an equal-valued intermediate fraction from a fully reduced endpoint. No fixed paragraph header, copied source order, step count or new alloy renderer is proposed.

design.mechanism: One shared content semantics maintains integer numerator/denominator identity through multiplication, exact simultaneous cancellation, division with remainder, equivalence assertions and a claimed greatest common measure or fully reduced result. Paths may differ in operation order and length while denoting one rational value. Coprimeness/maximality is an additional meaningful condition, not implied by endpoint value equality.
design.unit: A whole bounded rational calculation/argument, including problem, each path, intermediate assertions, explanations and declared endpoint qualification. The complete historical source subsection is retained; a future complete target grammar must preserve every admitted meaning clause rather than treat explanation as filler. No source item count equals a target group count.
design.contrast: GDT909 already tests Euclidean-style dividend/divisor/remainder transfers under at-least-three equal-width steps with four single-group roles; it is not reopened. New proposed content consequence is alternative value-preserving calculation plus the separately asserted greatest/common-factor or lowest-terms endpoint. GDT902 fixed copied multiplication and GDT969 generated root-trace writers remain closed; no new template is substituted.

historical_source.text_policy: Raw layout OCR, not diplomatic transcription: original numeric/fraction and letter errors preserved. Page header/footer and marginal apparatus are not semantic events. Native numerical observations below override OCR only where specifically stated; uncertain fraction digits remain uncertain.

complete_source_content_inventory: Multiply220 by147 and divide by the written fractional denominators; state whole449 plus compound remainder notation and a pensa0 per11.
Interpret compound remainder through1*8+4=12 and8*9=72; reduce12/72 to1/6; explain proportional parts with Euclid reference.
Alternative: take147/3=49 and220/4=55; multiply; divide by9/3=3 and8/4=2, hence by6; obtain the same449+1/6.
General reduction: divide numerator and denominator by greatest common measure; explicitly place the resulting numerator above and denominator below the bar.
Written elementary reductions6/9 to2/3 and5/10 to1/2.

General common-measure procedure: divide larger by smaller; exact-division base case; name first residue and divide smaller by it; name second residue if necessary; continue the stated larger/smaller divisions until an exact one, declaring the common measure greatest and citing Euclid.
Worked pair22,10: remainder2, then10 is exactly divisible by2.
Worked pair20,12: remainder8;12 divided by8 leaves4;12 is then exactly divisible by4.

retained_uncertainties: The base-case stacked fraction in the general rule has not had all digits independently resolved; retained in raw OCR/native render rather than silently filled.
Source general larger/smaller reference ownership is not a ready-made unambiguous register update.
The worked20/12 example explicitly checks12/4, not a silently repaired8/4.
The source pensa0 per11 assertion is retained; its convention is not fully reconstructed here.
Euclid proof/prerequisite citation is retained, not newly acquired or expanded.
OCR149 in the cancellation discussion is read as147 from native print; source147/3=49 supports but does not replace that inspection.

complete_generated_example.claim: Both paths preserve value and end coprime; stopping pathB at14/21 fails only the full-reduction claim.

constraints: CANCEL(k,a,b) requires k>0 integer and exact divisibility of both a and b; replace by a/k,b/k.
Fractions retain ordered numerator and denominator and one globally shared numeric interpretation.
Division relation a=q*b+r has nonnegative integer q,r and0<=r<b.
A common-measure claim divides both original integers; a greatest claim additionally needs a complete certificate.
FULLY_REDUCED(a,b) requires gcd(a,b)=1 and value preservation relative the initial expression.
semantic_kernel.procedure_policy: A standard decreasing-current-pair remainder kernel is a modern explicit option, not a claim that the source prose already supplies its exact serializer. No source-reference ambiguity is silently repaired.
semantic_kernel.writing_policy: Unknown, no target code supplied. A later finite shared compositional grammar may vary statement/explanation lengths and jointly infer constituents and quantities. No fixed header, step count, decimal/opcode field record or paragraph segmentation is selected.
